query: Which material can be used for improve the magnetocaloric properties, and why?

generation.hypothesis: The incorporation of specific rare-earth elements into magnetocaloric materials will enhance their magnetocaloric properties.
generation.material_initial_state: Base magnetocaloric material without rare-earth elements.
generation.intervention: Doping the base magnetocaloric material with rare-earth elements.
generation.conditions: Controlled temperature and magnetic field variations during testing.
generation.structural_mediator: Crystal structure and magnetic ordering of the doped material.
generation.mechanism: The rare-earth elements modify the magnetic interactions and entropy changes in the material.
generation.predicted_outcome: Increased magnetocaloric effect compared to the base material.
generation.baseline: Magnetocaloric properties of the base material without doping.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis is limited to the effects of rare-earth element doping on magnetocaloric materials.
generation.uncertainty: The specific rare-earth elements that will provide the most significant enhancement are not identified.

falsification_experiment.design: Conduct experiments comparing the magnetocaloric properties of the base material and the doped material under identical conditions.
measurements: Magnetocaloric effect (ΔT) under varying magnetic fields
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the doped material does not show a statistically significant increase in magnetocaloric effect compared to the base material, the hypothesis is falsified.
